records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed, accepted BMC Nursing article published online as an unedited Article in Press on 29 July 2026; DOI 10.1186/s12912-026-05085-x; accepted 15 July 2026; Version of Record edits pending
records.decision_reason: The official 59-page accepted manuscript directly compares a separately completed human reflexive thematic analysis with a two-cycle GPT-5.5 analysis of the same Chinese interviews and reflexively analyzes convergence, contextual loss, and ethical implications.

Research objective.value: Compare human-led reflexive thematic analysis and ChatGPT-assisted thematic analysis of the same nursing interview dataset and examine methodological advantages, limitations, and ethical concerns.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: secondary qualitative analysis using parallel human reflexive thematic analysis and ChatGPT-assisted thematic analysis

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Nineteen Chinese nursing stakeholders were interviewed for a broader platform project. The team first completed inductive Braun-and-Clarke-style reflexive thematic analysis; separately, one-to-two anonymized transcripts per batch were submitted once to GPT-5.5 in Chinese for summary, initial codes, subthemes, and themes, followed by a second clarification/refinement cycle. Only after both pathways were complete did the team compare codes, themes, descriptions, and selected excerpts and reflexively construct four ethical themes.
Actual operationalized methodology.anchor: Chronology and Human-AI Comparative Analysis, pp. 10-11

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: inductive parallel analyses followed by comparative/reflexive synthesis
Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.anchor: initial codes were subsequently developed inductively, p. 9

Domain.value: nursing research data platforms, AI-assisted qualitative inquiry, and Traditional Chinese Medicine nursing

Dataset name.value: secondary interviews from the Shenzhen Bao'an Public Hospital specialty-specific TCM nursing intervention database platform project

Public or restricted data.value: restricted; full transcripts withheld because of confidentiality and re-identification risk; anonymized excerpts are published
Public or restricted data.anchor: Availability of data and materials, p. 25

Number of documents.anchor: A total of 19 nursing personnel, p. 5

Number of participants.value: 19 nursing personnel and research stakeholders from one Shenzhen tertiary integrated Chinese/Western medicine hospital

Approximate corpus size.value: 19 interviews, each approximately 30-60 minutes; exact word/token count not reported
Approximate corpus size.anchor: Each interview lasted approximately 30-60 minutes, p. 7

Language.value: Chinese for interviews, transcripts, human analysis, and ChatGPT analysis; representative quotations translated into English only after theme development

Sensitive-data status.value: confidential, potentially identifiable health-workforce interview data
Sensitive-data status.anchor: Availability of data and materials, p. 25

Exact model/version.value: the ChatGPT web interface displayed GPT-5.5 during analysis, 30 May-5 June 2026

Prompting strategy.value: same general transcript-grounded thematic-analysis prompt across one-to-two-transcript batches, followed by a second clarification/organization/refinement cycle; representative prompts are supplied in Supplementary File 2

Single-agent or multi-agent.value: single ChatGPT analyst contrasted with a human research team

Human role.value: Researchers independently conducted the human reflexive analysis before AI comparison, checked and anonymized transcripts, documented prompts/outputs, reviewed rather than accepted AI outputs, compared both pathways, reflected on positionality, and constructed final ethical themes.

Unit of analysis.value: interview transcript, initial code, preliminary theme, theme description, and selected excerpt
Unit of analysis.anchor: comparison was conducted at the level of initial codes, preliminary themes, theme descriptions, and interpretations of selected excerpts, p. 10

Generated outputs.value: AI summaries, initial codes, preliminary subthemes/themes, human-led themes, human-AI comparison tables, and four final ethical themes with eight subthemes

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: audit trail of anonymized transcripts, coding records, theme notes, prompts, AI outputs, and comparison tables; published participant-ID excerpts support themes

Baselines.value: separately completed human reflexive thematic analysis of the identical dataset

Number of runs or seeds.value: each transcript batch analyzed once; the same batch was not intentionally regenerated; exact number of web sessions was not prospectively recorded; no seed or decoding settings reported
Number of runs or seeds.anchor: exact number of ChatGPT web sessions was not prospectively recorded, p. 9

Automatic metrics.value: none; comparison was qualitative and reflexive rather than score-based
Automatic metrics.anchor: Human-led interpretations were not treated as an objective reference standard, pp. 10-11

Human-evaluation design.value: At least two researchers independently reviewed transcripts, preliminary codes, and emerging themes; differences were discussed in regular team meetings. Human and AI pathways were compared only after each was developed, across codes, themes, descriptions, and excerpts.

Number and expertise of evaluators.value: at least two independent reviewers within a six-author team spanning clinical nursing, nursing management/education/research, qualitative research, and TCM nursing; exact reviewer allocation per item is not reported

Inter-rater reliability.value: not reported and not treated as an objective target under reflexive thematic analysis
Inter-rater reliability.anchor: human interpretations were not treated as an objective reference standard, p. 10

Statistical analysis.anchor: comparative and reflexive analytic process, p. 11

Principal results.value: Both pathways identified explicit issues, but researchers judged GPT-5.5 outputs semantically coherent yet contextually simplified, particularly for emotional, tacit, relational, and culturally embedded TCM meanings. Comparative synthesis produced four ethical themes: privacy/data security; loss of contextual/emotional understanding; algorithmic reductionism/cultural bias; and changing researcher roles/responsibilities.

Efficiency or cost results.value: Authors observed faster organization/preliminary exploration, but did not collect time, cost, or workload data and note additional anonymization, checking, contextual verification, and reflexive work

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Ethics approval KY-2026-102-01, written consent and withdrawal rights; direct and indirect identifiers removed/generalized before ChatGPT; AI outputs critically reviewed for misrepresentation; COREQ reporting; chat history and Memory were enabled, but vendor retention/governance settings are not described.
Ethics and privacy treatment.anchor: Ethical Considerations, p. 13; AI-Assisted Thematic Analysis, p. 9

Reproducibility resources.value: supplements include full interview guide, AI protocol/representative prompts, and COREQ checklist; internal audit trail retained; exact session count, decoding settings, full transcripts, and executable code are unavailable

Author-reported limitations.value: One model, one prompt protocol, one Chinese nursing dataset/cultural context; no measured time/cost/workload; rapidly changing models; reflexive findings shaped by researcher positionality; exact web-session count not recorded.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: the six-author research team is both the human analytic condition and the judge of which human interpretation is more contextually grounded, without an independent evaluator, member checking, or systematic completeness/error rubric. Small-group and individual interviews are mixed, no field notes/transcript return occurred, session state had chat history and Memory enabled, and unrecorded sessions/settings prevent reconstruction. The final ethical themes combine participant views, analyst-output differences, and researchers' normative interpretation, so they are not direct participant-prevalence findings.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Material qualitative counterpoint to agreement-based benchmarks: it operationalizes interpretive divergence, cultural/contextual loss, audit trails, and explicit non-equivalence without treating human themes as objective gold, while revealing the need for independent comparative adjudication.
Relevance to the proposed ARR project.anchor: Human-led interpretations were not treated as an objective reference standard, p. 10
